#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST="backup-srv:/srv/nightly"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

# Cron may invoke this script from an arbitrary working directory.  Keep both
# the input logs and the locally created tarball relative to this script.
SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/
scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -eu
sh -n backup.sh
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$work/logs" "$work/bin"
printf 'nightly log\n' > "$work/logs/app.log"
cp backup.sh "$work/backup.sh"
cat > "$work/bin/scp" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
[ "$1" = "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" ]
[ "$2" = "backup-srv:/srv/nightly/" ]
printf '%s\n' "$*" > scp.args
EOF
chmod +x "$work/bin/scp"
(
  cd "$work"
  PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" ./backup.sh
  test -f "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
  tar -tzf "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" | grep -Fx 'logs/app.log'
  test "$(cat scp.args)" = "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz backup-srv:/srv/nightly/"
)
printf 'backup.sh syntax and local packaging/copy invocation test passed\n'
